A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WaveGC research despite the changed title and substantial revision. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original WaveGC benchmark results, component ablations, sensitivity analyses and heterophily experiments in the main text and Appendix D.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark results, component and scale analyses, runtime measurements and experiments evaluating its simplified variant in Appendices C and D.

M1.justification: The main Chebyshev decomposition and shared matrix-valued kernels remain. However, v2 Appendix D introduces an evaluated eigendecomposition-free variant using Laplacian polynomial operations and a window approximation for scaled wavelets, while removing eigenvalue encoding and tight-frame constraints. This is a substantial additional computational procedure; the hybrid architecture itself already appeared in v1 as GraphGPS+WaveGC.

E1.justification: The ten main short-range and long-range datasets remain, but v1 Appendix D.5's Actor, Minesweeper and Tolokers experiments disappear entirely. This removes the distinct heterophily evaluation coverage. V2's additional scale and approximation experiments use retained datasets.

E2.justification: The main comparisons shift from Transformer and polynomial GNN baselines toward wavelet and scattering methods, adding Scattering, Scattering GCN, UFGConvS/R, WaveShrink-ChebNet, WaveNet and SEA-GWNN. The controlled Transformer/SAN/GraphGPS replacement comparisons disappear. SGWT, GWNN and DEFT were already evaluated in v1; v2 expands their participation. Appendix D additionally evaluates BernNet and UniFilter alongside GPRGNN.

E3.justification: Evaluation shifts from three backbone integrations to one hybrid configuration. Comparing v1 Table 15's GraphGPS+WaveGC settings with v2 Table 13, Computer changes from rho=3 to 7 and scale bounds from {1,1,1} to {10,10,10}; ogbn-arxiv and Peptides-struct settings also change. New analyses introduce a threshold-defined receptive-field measure and extreme scale bounds. These are reported setting changes, not proof that particular experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds learned-scale/receptive-field analyses, extreme-scale visualizations, independent coefficient and scale ablations, timing analyses and evaluation of the simplified approximation. Its hybrid-component ablations replace v1's backbone-combination study and explicit tight-frame ablation results. The CoraFull full/partial-spectrum visualizations are retained, rather than newly added.

E5.justification: V1 Appendix D.1 and v2 Appendix C.1 both specify ten short-range runs and four long-range runs, reporting means and standard deviations. Neither introduces a new seed protocol, confidence interval or significance-testing procedure. Additional result rows follow existing reporting practices.

E6.justification: Many benchmark and diagnostic entries are added, removed or revised. For example, v1 Table 2's GraphGPS+WaveGC row reports Computer accuracy 91.00 and Peptides-struct MAE 24.95; v2's hybrid reports 92.26 and 24.83 under revised settings, so these are not established same-setting gains. New approximation and timing results appear, while heterophily results disappear. The sensitivity plots also change: the best Peptides-struct rho moves from 2 to 3, although v2's prose still says 2.

T1.justification: V1 Theorem 4.3's one-hop comparison becomes v2 Theorem 4.2's K-order message-passing comparison, with revised bounds and an expanded Appendix A.3 derivation. V1's explicit vanishing-derivative assumption is removed, and Appendix A.1 introduces a multi-order Taylor expansion and a new mu quantity. The Transformer-convolution derivation is removed, while Appendix D adds polynomial and window-function derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction refocus superiority claims from graph convolutions and Transformers to existing graph wavelet techniques. The contribution of improving three Transformer backbones, including the claimed 26.20% CoraFull and 9.21% VOC improvements, is replaced by a wavelet-focused comparison claiming 15.7% on VOC. The central admissibility and short-/long-range separation claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 replaces v1's frequency-interaction rationale for the kernel with an explanation based on localized wavelet coefficients. It expands interpretation of spectral truncation, learned scales and complementary MPNN information, and attributes receptive-field flexibility specifically to scale rather than polynomial order. Computational limitations now distinguish eigendecomposition from training and discuss the approximation's accuracy tradeoff; the earlier heterophily and dataset-dependent tight-frame interpretations disappear.

D1.justification: V2 adds training/eigendecomposition timings, per-epoch resource measurements and SGWT/Scattering adaptation details. Its configuration table is reduced to one backbone, updates hyperparameters and omits the per-dataset cross-layer parameter-sharing flags supplied in v1. The PyTorch implementation, stated hardware and code-access URL remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Research positioning shifts substantially toward graph wavelets and scattering. Appendix E adds dedicated graph-scattering and spectral-convolution discussions, including works such as Scattering GCN, WaveNet and SEA-GWNN, while greatly reducing the Transformer survey. The kernel discussion is reframed around Fourier/wavelet neural operators rather than the previous Transformer-equivalence derivation.

P1.justification: V2 changes the title, substantially rewrites the kernel rationale and experimental narrative, and reverses the order of the basis and kernel subsections. It reorganizes the appendices, removes the Transformer derivation and backbone descriptions, and introduces dedicated complexity and approximation sections. These changes substantially alter the paper's explanatory structure.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column to a two-column layout. Figure 1 is rearranged, Figure 2 changes comparator panels, and the three-backbone illustration becomes a single hybrid diagram. New receptive-field and scale/window diagrams and runtime tables accompany extensive restructuring of benchmark and configuration tables. The retained CoraFull visualizations are primarily relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens focused empirical support through broader wavelet comparisons, targeted ablations, runtime reporting and an evaluated eigendecomposition-free variant, while reducing Transformer and heterophily validation breadth. However, the theoretical revision leaves a substantive gap: after removing v1's vanishing-derivative assumption and introducing lower-order terms in Eq. (16), v2 still uses a pure Kth-order expression in Eq. (29). The empirical benefits and unresolved reliability of the revised central theory prevent a confident net-quality judgment.
